clue.text: Possibly inaccurate, but right for new cartoon?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged some other way to give a new word
right for new means R takes the place of N in the word inaccurate

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a newspaper cartoon is a little unfair to its subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right for new' swaps the N of INACCURATE for an R, and 'Possibly' then rearranges the resulting letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A caricature is an exaggerated comic drawing of a person, the stock-in-trade of a newspaper cartoonist.

clue.text: One escaping head cook

indicators.note: the one getting away from the word for head means that letter is taken out

parts.note: a chief is a head or leader
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A kitchen boss runs away from the restaurant.
explanation.definitionFit: A chef is a professional cook in a restaurant kitchen.

clue.text: Painter showing back in bizarre portrait

indicators.note: showing back says the letters are read from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the words bizarre portrait

explanation.surface: An artist exhibits from behind in a strange likeness.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading EPOR across 'bizarrE PORtrait' backwards gives the word. 'Painter' is not an artist here: on a boat it is the line used to tie up.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is a mooring line attached to the bow of a small boat.

clue.text: One's pushed out and given the brush-off in sport

definitions.text: One's pushed out and given the brush-off in sport

parts.words: One's pushed out and given the brush-off in sport
parts.note: a heavy granite object is slid along ice while teammates sweep the ice ahead of it with brooms, so it literally gets brushed

explanation.surface: Someone is rejected and snubbed in an athletic setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given the brush-off' reads as being snubbed, but in the Scottish ice game the sweepers literally brush the ice in front of the sliding stone.
explanation.definitionFit: In curling, players push a heavy polished stone across the ice while sweepers brush its path.

clue.text: Powers support most of article

parts.note: a tee is the peg that supports a golf ball

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the word for article is dropped

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Authority backs up the greater part of a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A law or body with teeth has real force, so the word means effective powers.

clue.text: Particular people run in socks -I run in shoes!

parts.note: a race is a particular people or ethnic group

indicators.note: in says the letter for run goes inside the word for socks

parts.note: hose is an old word for stockings or socks
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A runner contrasts others jogging in socks with racing properly shod.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the animal speaking: it runs wearing horseshoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A thoroughbred galloper on the turf wears iron horseshoes when it competes.

clue.text: Fairy-tale writer avoiding ending that's depressing

indicators.note: avoiding ending tells us to drop the last letter of the writer's name

parts.note: the brothers Grimm collected German fairy tales

explanation.surface: A storyteller shies away from a sad conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: Grim and depressing are synonyms describing a bleak, gloomy outlook.

clue.text: Greg's extremities in lather, suffering? It's 90%!

indicators.note: suffering suggests something put through torment and so twisted out of shape
extremities are the first and last letters of the name Greg

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Greg is in a sweat and in pain, apparently at full stretch.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of Greg, the word 'in' and LATHER are rearranged together, signalled by 'suffering'. The '%' stands for the degree sign: the corner is ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: A corner of exactly ninety degrees, as in a square, is the geometric figure meant.

clue.text: Unpleasant of French to call without coming to the point

parts.note: mean can describe nasty or unkind behaviour
de is the French word for of
to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A rude remark about telephoning the French, made in a roundabout way.
explanation.definitionFit: Meandering talk wanders around and fails to get to the main issue.

clue.text: Feel passion returning when apprehended by old coppers

parts.note: ex means former or old

indicators.note: apprehended by casts the old coppers as police arresting the passion, so it sits inside them

parts.note: pence are copper coins

indicators.note: returning means the word for passion is read backwards

parts.note: ire is anger, a strong passion

explanation.surface: Anger comes back when one is arrested by former policemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police but means copper coins. 'returning' turns IRE into ERI, which goes inside EX + PENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To experience something is to feel or undergo it.

clue.text: Muslim commander imprisoning king in Indian city

indicators.note: imprisoning means the commander's title holds the king's letter inside it

parts.note: an aga is an Ottoman or Muslim military commander
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An Islamic leader jails a monarch in a city in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is the city in northern India home to the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Behaviour that's above board?

parts.note: above board usually means honest, but here it is literal: conduct shown over the dining table

explanation.surface: A question about honest, open conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Above board' means honest, but read literally it is how you behave over the board, the dining table.
explanation.definitionFit: Etiquette at meals is the polite conduct expected while eating at a dining table.

clue.text: Land, ploughed earth, arable ground ultimately without depth?

parts.note: to light is to land or settle, as a bird lights on a branch

indicators.note: ploughed earth is turned over, so its letters are churned up
ultimately picks the final letter of each of the words arable and ground

explanation.surface: A farming scene: land, tilled soil and finally a field of crops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ploughed' rearranges EARTH into HEART; 'ultimately' takes the last letters E and D of 'arable ground'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cheerful and frivolous lacks seriousness, so is not deep.

clue.text: An act with cross, possibly of a devotional nature

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters could be put together another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gesture of crossing oneself, perhaps a religious one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacrosanct means sacred or holy and so treated with religious reverence.

clue.text: Rich vocal arrangement with dead keyboard instrument

indicators.note: arrangement suggests a musical setting, but signals the letters being reordered

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for dead, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A full-voiced choral arrangement accompanied by an old keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The clavichord is an early stringed instrument played from a keyboard, a forerunner of the piano.

clue.text: Reptile masquerading as a log with tail, right?

indicators.note: masquerading means disguised, so the letters appear in another form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature lying in a river disguised as a floating log.
explanation.definitionFit: The alligator is a large crocodilian reptile of American and Chinese rivers.

clue.text: Source of food cooked for a mutt, right? For a mog, surely!

indicators.note: cooked suggests preparing a meal but signals the letters being rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Pet food made for a dog, though a cat would surely prefer it.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing 'For a mog, surely!' adds a cat's view: a fish farm would be a feast for a moggy (British slang for a cat).
explanation.definitionFit: A fish farm breeding trout supplies fish to eat.

clue.text: Individual caught between two sides?

indicators.note: caught between places the word for individual inside the two side letters

parts.note: L and R are left and right, the two sides
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Someone caught in the middle of a dispute between factions.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a lone individual sits between left and right, belonging to neither side.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person who avoids company keeps apart from groups on either side.

clue.text: Fix hedge, clipping front

indicators.note: clipping front means the first letter of the hedge is cut off

parts.note: privet is a common hedging shrub

explanation.surface: A gardener mends a hedge by trimming its face.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet is to fasten or fix firmly, as with metal pins.

clue.text: Zero information given to me, beginning to live on fruit

parts.note: O looks like zero
gen is British slang for information
taken as written

indicators.note: beginning to picks the first letter of the word live

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone told nothing decides to start living on fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ogen is a small sweet melon variety first developed in Israel.

clue.text: Almost 1300 hours when name's brought in? Excellent

indicators.note: brought in means the letter for name is put inside the phrase

parts.note: 1300 hours is one o'clock, so a moment before it is a second to one
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Something happens at nearly one in the afternoon when someone's name is introduced.
explanation.walkthrough: Insert N into SECOND TO ONE, one second before 1300 hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unbeaten by any rival is supremely good, the best there is.

clue.text: Pacific territory, note, linked to gold and rugby

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
RU stands for Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A Pacific land associated with music, gold and rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Nauru is a small island nation in the Pacific Ocean, in Micronesia.

clue.text: Greek character going to doctor, having lost feeling

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
MB is a Bachelor of Medicine degree, so a doctor

explanation.surface: A Greek visits the doctor after losing sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: Numb means deprived of sensation, so without feeling.

clue.text: Very attractive and certainly accepting kiss when getting up

indicators.note: in a down clue getting up means the letters are read from bottom to top
accepting means the word for certainly takes the kiss inside it

parts.note: yes is an emphatic certainly
X stands for a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: An attractive person agrees to a kiss on rising.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes inside YES to make YXES, and 'getting up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexy describes someone strongly attractive or alluring.

clue.text: No cricket side appearing in hottest part of day?

parts.note: on is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team fails to turn up in the midday heat.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the ON side, also called the leg side, is the half of the field behind the batter's legs.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday, when the sun is at its highest, is usually the hottest time.

clue.text: Non-medicinal treatment's slapdash care? Untrue

indicators.note: slapdash means careless and haphazard, so the letters are thrown together anyhow

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses drug-free therapy as sloppy and false.
explanation.definitionFit: This is healing through diet, rest and natural means rather than drugs.

clue.text: Activity also involving daughter

indicators.note: involving means the word for also contains the letter for daughter

parts.note: too means also

explanation.surface: A family affair that includes a daughter too.
explanation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or fuss, a flurry of activity.

clue.text: Something unexpected in store for you?

definitions.text: Something unexpected in store for you?

parts.words: Something unexpected in store for you?
parts.note: in store for you usually means awaiting you in future, but here it is literally a purchase made on a whim in a shop

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller's warning of a surprise to come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In store for you' sounds like a prophecy but means literally in a shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A spontaneous shop purchase made on a whim, unplanned in advance.
